pageCache.pageTitle: St Leonard's C.E. Primary School – Where Everyone Matters
pageCache.text:
Welcome to St Leonard’s! Don’t forget to visit our Facebook page to see all the exciting things happening in our school. Click here for a direct link.
Head Teacher’s Welcome
It is a pleasure to welcome you to St Leonard’s Church of England Primary School where we are proud to serve our local community.
Our Christian vision to prepare children for “Life in All its Fullness” (John, 10:10) is bearing fruit. Our engaging and inspiring curriculum encourages curious and resilient learners; our aim is that children become life long learners and have a place in the community where they can thrive.
At the same time we have not lost sight of our core values of Love, Respect and Responsibility. Right from their first steps into Nursery and Reception our children are nurtured as unique individuals and are friendly and well behaved. The St Leonard’s Way is planned to Engage, Challenge and Inspire young minds making school a fun, safe and stimulating place to learn.
We are very fortunate to have the most amazing, spacious grounds where children can explore and learn about their immediate environment.
We have fantastic staff who are not only talented and dedicated to the children at St Leonard’s, but who nurture and bring out the best in all children.
We hope that you find our website useful and informative. It is intended to keep existing families up to date and to give potential new families a taster of life at St Leonard’s.
If you are seeking a place for your child, either now or in the future, then please telephone or email to arrange a visit and see for yourself our happy, wonderful school.

pageCache.pageTitle: Early Years Curriculum – St Leonard's C.E. Primary School
pageCache.text:
Early Years Curriculum
At St. Leonard’s we wish to engage, challenge and inspire children from the very beginning of their learning journey. Our Early Years Education is carefully structured within a well organised, safe and enabling environment, offering children rich and stimulating experiences, building on what children already know and providing opportunities to develop what they need to know next.
Through a careful balance of child initiated, adult initiated and adult led activities we aim to encourage independence, self-regulation, cooperation, creativity, communication and problem solving. We plan an exciting and challenging curriculum based on our observation of children’s needs, interests and next steps. We use stories and rhymes as the basis for our planning, which means that by the end of Reception children will have encountered a wide range of high quality texts to inspire a lifetime love of reading.
For more information about our Early Years Curriculum please see the long term plan below.

pageCache.pageTitle: Reception – St Leonard's C.E. Primary School
pageCache.text:
Reception
Children starting Reception have their whole school journey ahead of them, and we aim to get them off to a flying start. Through child initiated learning in our exciting and stimulating indoor and outdoor classroom and carefully planned adult led sessions and activities, children are challenged and engaged in their learning.
A Typical Day in Reception
8.55am – Group Time. This is usually Literacy based and will be an introduction to the adult led activity and learning environment.
9.15am – Children have access to the learning environment (indoors and out) as well as completing adult led activities.
11am – Phonics Group Time.
12.30pm – Afternoon Register and Maths Group Time.
12.55pm -Children have access to the learning environment (indoors and out) as well as completing adult led activities.
2.40pm – Group Time. This may be a story, music, circle time, singing, sharing homework, discussing school values or a topic session.
We also offer Breakfast and After School Club, details can be found here.
How To Apply
Children are eligible to start in our Reception class in the September of the academic year that they turn 5 years old. Admissions are managed by Oxfordshire County Council, applications open in the October/November with the deadline for applying in January.
All information regarding this and the online application form can be found at www.oxfordshire.gov.uk
If your child attends our Nursery you must also apply for a Reception place through this process. Attending our Nursery does not automatically secure your child’s Reception place.
If you require a place in our Reception class during the academic year, you must apply to Oxfordshire County Council by filling in the In Year Transfer form.
If you need any further information or would like to speak to our Early Years Leader of Learning, you can contact the School Office.
telephone 01295 262507 email office.3262@st-leonards.oxon.sch.uk

pageCache.pageTitle: UKS2 Residential June 2026 – St Leonard's C.E. Primary School
pageCache.text:
The children started off at Youlbury Scout Camp enjoying abseiling, archery and flying down the zip wire. The children then settled into their accommodation at Hill End.
The following day they studied the habitat of the meadow, pond and woodland where they then had the opportunity to do some den building.
Later in the day they went on a scavenger hunt using their orienteering and decoding skills.
On the final day they learnt survival skills and they were taught how to identify which plants were safe to eat or which were poisonous. The children then had a go at building shelters and making fires.

St Leonard’s CE School Governing Board Vision
As a Church School, St Leonard’s provides love, care and support for all its families, nurturing children as individuals and as learners so that they are able to become valuable citizens within wider society – preparing children for “life in all its fullness” (John 10:10)
St. Leonard’s Church of England Primary School works with our local community for the benefit of all its children and their families. We strive to provide a safe, happy and stimulating learning environment where children and adults alike treat each other with Love, Respect and Responsibility. A caring Christian ethos supports learning in order to realise children’s potential, both as learners and as citizens. The School creates a positive moral framework, ensuring diversity is respected, and everyone is treated with fairness and tolerance. We aim to broaden children’s horizons and expectations, build resilience and self-confidence, and prepare children for their next steps in education and as members of British society. We do this through the ‘St Leonard’s Way’ – where children are Challenged, Engaged and Inspired; we want our pupils to be proud of who they are and what they have achieved, have aspirations for their future, a can-do attitude, and a growth mindset. Above all, we aim to teach our children to embrace ‘Life in all its Fullness’.
We expect our staff, pupils and parents to follow our School Values, which are based on teachings from the Bible:
These values and the School’s Christian vision are shared through lessons, assemblies, and collective worship, and are embedded in the whole ethos of our School and the way we behave towards one another. We welcome all faiths and backgrounds equally, and work to ensure children grow without prejudice.
The Governing Board of St. Leonard’s aims to ensure the School delivers the best education and life preparation it can for its pupils. We base our work on the following actions and principles:
Governing Board Priorities 2026–27
At St Leonard’s, our Governing Board is committed to supporting the school in providing the very best education and opportunities for every child. During the 2026–27 academic year, our key priorities are:
1. Supporting Strong Leadership
We work closely with the Headteacher and Senior Leadership Team, providing both support and constructive challenge to help ensure the school continues to thrive. Our focus is on making decisions that benefit pupils, staff and the wider school community.
2. Delivering Excellence in Education
We are committed to ensuring that every child receives a high-quality education. Governors monitor pupil progress, celebrate success and work with school leaders to address challenges, helping all pupils achieve their full potential.
3. Championing Inclusion and Opportunity
We believe every child should have the opportunity to succeed. We monitor how the school supports pupils with Special Educational Needs and Disabilities (SEND), as well as those facing other barriers to learning. We also oversee the effective use of Pupil Premium and PE and Sport Premium funding, ensuring all children can access enriching experiences, clubs, trips and wider opportunities.
4. Promoting Good Attendance
Regular attendance is essential for learning and wellbeing. We support the school in working positively with families to overcome barriers to attendance and ensure that every child can benefit fully from school life.
5. Maintaining a Broad and Ambitious Curriculum
Governors oversee the development of a rich, engaging and inclusive curriculum that reflects the diversity of our community. Alongside strong foundations in reading, writing and mathematics, we want every child to enjoy a wide range of learning experiences that inspire curiosity and achievement.
6. Strengthening Community Engagement
We are proud of our inclusive school community and value our partnerships with families, local organisations and the wider community. Governors support the school in building strong relationships that help every child feel valued, supported and able to succeed.
7. Effective Governance and Sustainability
We are committed to ensuring that the school is well-led, financially secure and focused on continuous improvement. Governors provide strategic oversight, ensuring resources are used effectively and that sustainability remains an important consideration in future planning.
8. Supporting Staff Wellbeing and Development
Our staff are central to the success of the school. We encourage professional development, recognise the dedication of our team and support a positive working environment where staff wellbeing is valued. By investing in our staff, we help ensure the best possible outcomes for our pupils.

pageCache.pageTitle: School Lunches – St Leonard's C.E. Primary School
pageCache.text:
School Lunches
DOLCE supply our school dinners here at St Leonard’s and are determined to offer you and your child an excellent service, ensuring every child enjoys their meal and has the energy to study and learn in the afternoon.
The cost of a school dinner will be £2.72 per day (£13.60 per week) or £2.60 a day for Nursery children.
Our Menu
SchoolGrid Account
When your child starts school you will be sent an email to create a SchoolGrid account. By accessing SchoolGrid online you will be able to pre order meals, view recipes, allergens, ingredients and make payments.
Allergies
All allergies must be added to your SchoolGrid account, if you are having difficulties ticking the allergen information you need, please contact Customer Care on the contact details listed below and they will happily make arrangements to accommodate your child’s individual needs.
Payments
Your SchoolGrid account must be kept in credit. You can top your account up by:
Online Card Payment – A card payment can be made online through your SchoolGrid account, please log on and select [Account] – [Pay by card] where on screen prompts will assist in taking payment.
Telephone Card Payment – Our Customer Care team is available 8.00 am to 5.00 pm Monday to Friday to take a card payment for your account on 01942 707709. The minimum payment amount we can accept over the phone is £10.
Free Meals
If your child is in Reception/KS1 then you are entitled to Universal Free School meals. This will automatically be set up on your account as free, all the other features can be used as normal. If your child is in Nursery/KS2, you may still be entitled to Free School Meals so please contact the school office to find out if you are eligible. Once a decision has been made, we will update your account to Free School Meals.
Contact Details
Dolce is your catering provider. If you have any questions, comments or suggestions regarding school meals, allergens, payments etc, please do not hesitate to contact Dolce Customer Care Monday to Friday 8am to 5pm, on 01942 707709 or by email to customercare@dolce.co.uk, we are always happy to hear from you.
SchoolGrid is the Software provider we use. If you experience any technical issues with access to SchoolGrid, please contact SchoolGrid technical support on 01506 300310 or by email to support@schoolgrid.co.uk
Packed Lunches
If your child does not want to stay for school dinners, they can choose to bring a packed lunch from home. We strongly encourage healthy food and drink options, examples of this can be found on the links below.
NHS – Healthier lunchbox recipes
BBC Goodfood – Healthy Lunchbox Ideas

pageCache.pageTitle: SEND Information – St Leonard's C.E. Primary School
pageCache.text:
SEND Information
St Leonard’s Primary School is a mainstream school in the heart of Banbury. Currently 15% of our school have special educational needs or disability (SEND) inline with other schools nationally. Pupils with SEND, along with all pupils, have entitlement to the greatest possible access to a broad and balanced curriculum, which at St Leonard’s is based upon the National Curriculum. This entitlement is an integral part of the school’s equality policy. All children should be given access to educational experiences of the highest quality and have the opportunity to develop into confident and independent learners. The achievements of children who have SEND are celebrated equally with those who find success easier to attain. We aim to ensure that children with SEND are perceived positively by all members of the school community, and that SEND and inclusive provision are positively valued and provided by all staff. At St Leonard’s Primary School, every teacher is a teacher of every child including those with SEND.
Aims
In class support includes:
Our teachers keep parents regularly informed about pupil’s progress. Parents are invited to share in achievements through Dojo points, certificates and rewards during assembly, school reports, parents’ evenings, newsletters and letters home.
effective use of visuals and ICT
effective use of manipulatives to support learning
use of the Zones of Regulation.
Examples of Support for Pupils at St Leonard’s
Following training from our Speech and Language link team, we are now able to offer six week programmes of Lego Therapy to small groups or pairs of children during school time for thirty minutes each week.
You may have read about Lego Therapy online as it has become quite a popular intervention in schools for developing a range of skills. Lego Therapy involves children taking on different roles to create a LEGO model together and is a very popular intervention among the children.
LEGO Therapy can be used to extend a range of skills including communication skills, cooperation, turn-taking, friendship skills and even to encourage quieter members of the class to take part in small group discussions. It is also great for developing teamwork, cooperation and self-confidence. Sometimes children are nominated to join a group because they will be a good role model for others.
If your child’s class teacher thinks that LEGO Therapy would be beneficial to your child, they will seek to secure them a place in the first instance before communicating with parents in more depth. Parents will then receive a letter with the option to opt out.
Little Wandle is a phonics intervention developed to support children who require further support in the acquisition of phonics knowledge. Pupils who require additional phonics learning time may receive intensive support from a trained member of staff.
WellComm is a Communication and Interaction package designed to help teachers support speech, language and communication needs within the classroom. WellComm is used in Early Years to screen pupils for possible language needs; it then generates personalised interventions to support aspects of language and communication development.
Throughout school, all children learn about developing their emotional literacy through the Zones of Regulation. The programme includes all children and they are taught the RULER approach to self regulation. Recognising, Understanding, Labelling, Expressing and finally Regulating their emotions.
Nurture and Welfare Support
At St Leonard’s, we have two members of staff dedicated to supporting nurture and wellbeing of all pupils who may require support. This can range from support for those suffering bereavements to developing children’s emotional literacy or improving social skills. We recognise that children learn better and are happier in school if their emotional needs are also addressed.

pageCache.pageTitle: Curriculum Statement – St Leonard's C.E. Primary School
pageCache.text:
Curriculum Statement
St Leonard’s curriculum is underpinned by our Christian vision to provide love, care and support for all its families, nurturing children as individuals and as learners, so that they are able to become valuable citizens within wider society; preparing children for “Life in All its Fullness” (John 10:10)
Our curriculum is designed to meet the unique needs of our demographic and context. We are a richly diverse and inclusive school, taking pupils from all parts of the world, with over 25 first languages spoken and a large proportion of EAL pupils. More than a quarter of our pupils are eligible for the pupil premium and our aim is to ensure that all children are able to flourish, irrespective of background.
Our current priority is that children are emotionally ready to learn, we are ensure that all children feel safe in order to be able to access learning. Pastoral care runs alongside learning throughout the school.
We strive to ensure that every child can communicate their thoughts and feelings. Early talk and the development of spoken language skills is a priority, with a whole school focus upon giving children a rich vocabulary with which to express themselves. Our intention is that every child becomes a reader, with phonics and early reading considered essential to giving children the skills needed to access learning and the world around them.
In order to learn deeply, we have an evolving, ambitious curriculum, designed to build upon children’s interests and give all learners, particularly the most disadvantaged and those with special educational needs and/or disabilities (SEND), the knowledge and cultural capital they need to succeed in life. Taking prior learning as our starting point, we ensure that activities give children the opportunity to know more, learn more and remember more than they did before.
To give purpose for learning, we complement the core skills of reading, writing and maths with a wide breadth of study in order to develop children’s vocabulary and interest in the world around them. Our pupils will have, by the end of each key stage, long-term retention of an ambitious body of skills and knowledge, and the social skills and responsibility needed to take their place in wider society.
Our curriculum is based upon the National Curriculum 2014 and Development Matters for EYFS 2023. It is topic based and each term children’s learning is based around a central theme. These themes are usually based around the History, Geography or Science curriculum. Topics include enquiry questions such as: When is a wood a forest? and Rules, Reformation and Royalty: how did the power of the monarchy change over time?
The curriculum offers a wide range of immersive experiences and allows children to be curious learners and question the world around them, building their cultural capital and vocabulary. Although much content is knowledge based, cross-curricular links ensure that learning is
interwoven across subjects and skills and knowledge are applied in a variety of contexts, giving purpose to learning and building connections and neural pathways.
It is important that the activities and tasks planned are real and relevant for the children and the St Leonard’s Way aims to Engage, Challenge and Inspire children of all abilities. Learning intentions are based upon the identified needs of the children and lessons always begin with extracting children’s prior knowledge about a concept so that there is a base of prior knowledge to build upon – often referred to as sticky knowledge. Lessons always end with an evaluation of what they have learned throughout the session, what helped them and how successful they have been, allowing children to become more practised at metacognition.
Children at St Leonard’s are encouraged to share their learning with others. They are able to challenge and support each other’s thinking, and sometimes their own, gaining a deeper understanding of the concepts and tasks studied.
To make learning as memorable as possible it is also supplemented by educational visits both local and further afield, residential visits in Key Stage 2, and visitors who include IMPS, SCIB workshops and members of local faith organisations such as St Leonard’s Church or Madni Masjid Mosque.
Alongside curriculum delivery, children are also taught how to learn and to develop a growth mind-set. To enable this, we use animal characters in EYFS to recognise and reinforce the Characteristics of Effective Learning and have developed a series of Learning Powers in the rest of the school. These have become a shared vocabulary of learning and our current Learning Powers are: Enjoy Learning, Be Co –Operative, Keep Improving, Use your imagination, Concentrate, Don’t Give up, Be Curious, Have a Go, Keep Flearning – learn from your mistakes, Try a challenge and Be Proud.
To supplement the curriculum, we have whole school themed events, these include: World Book Day; Maths Day; Science Week; Aspirations Week and Global Learning Week. These provide children with the chance to make connections in learning, and opportunities to share their work with other members of the school community and/or their families via assemblies, Class Dojo posts, learning afternoons and exhibitions.
The spiritual development of children is a priority and our school Christian values of Love, Respect, Responsibility run through the curriculum, supported by a varied programme of Collective Worship and Religious Education. Tolerance and respect of others’ differences and beliefs are actively promoted across our curriculum and Collective Worship sessions and we lay a strong foundation for British Values and participation in wider society.
Our PSHE and PE curriculums explore the importance of emotional and mental health and pupils are encouraged to look after this in the same way they are encouraged to look after their physical health. For pupils who need additional support, soft landings, nurture support and talk time is available. Parents can also contact our Home School Link Worker for any support related to family matters.
To support and extend the curriculum we offer a wide range of extra-curricular activities at lunchtime and after school, available throughout the year. Home Learning reinforces the curriculum and gives children options to develop, extend or consolidate learning completed within the classroom. For an overview of our curriculum, please see our Whole School Curriculum Plan.
Because learning is a change to long term memory, it is impossible to see impact in the short term. We know from cognitive science however that:
· Learning is most effective with spaced repetition
· Interleaving helps pupils to discriminate between topics and aids long-term retention.
· Frequent and regular retrieval of previously learned content increases both storage and retrieval strength.
We use whole class and ‘live’ feedback so that children know their strengths and have guidance on how to improve their work. Formal PiXL assessments facilitate comparative judgement of pupil’s work against 500+ schools nationally and allow us to identify areas of learning in which pupils are relatively strong and others which are areas for development and future learning.
The curriculum as a whole supports children to have the necessary knowledge, skills and attributes to make a successful transition to Secondary School and beyond. It runs alongside our aspirations work with children and families designed to raise ambitions for the future.
To find out more about our curriculum please see the Leaders of Learning: EYFS – Mrs T Pratley, KS1 – Mrs A Russell, LKS2 – Mrs L Wilson and UKS2 – Mrs R Lacey.
We follow the National Curriculum which sets out the framework for Key Stages 1 and 2. For more information please see the link below:
· National Curriculum – Key Stages One and Two
